domains.name: Flood monitoring
domains.summary: Dynamic flood maps from aerial imagery, updated as water spreads.

domains.name: Wildfire monitoring
domains.summary: RGB and thermal sensing to find fires early and follow their spread.

domains.name: Air pollution
domains.summary: Distributed sensing for high-resolution pollution maps.

domains.name: Water quality
domains.summary: Rivers, lakes and reservoirs monitored from above and at the surface.

domains.name: Forest and ecosystems
domains.summary: Vegetation and habitat tracking, including recovery after disasters.

domains.name: Landslides and land degradation
domains.summary: Terrain and vegetation change that signals unstable ground.

objectives.d: A distributed UAV sensing system that collects spatially and temporally resolved observations.
Lightweight models that detect anomalies and hazards close to the data source.
AI-based task allocation, area coverage, path planning and adaptive monitoring across UAVs.
Models that identify flooding, wildfire, pollution, landslides and ecosystem degradation.
Models that estimate how hazards may evolve and where they may spread.
A platform that combines UAV observations, edge-AI outputs, geospatial data and risk indicators.
A prototype evaluated in controlled and field-oriented monitoring scenarios.

layers.name: Environmental sensing
layers.d: RGB, thermal and multispectral cameras, atmospheric, temperature, humidity and water-quality sensors, plus positioning. Sensors are chosen per application.

layers.name: UAV swarm
layers.d: Multiple UAVs decide which area needs monitoring, which UAV goes, the best route, the priorities, and when to return for recharging or replacement.

layers.name: Edge computing
layers.d: Local image preprocessing, sensor fusion, hazard and anomaly detection, feature extraction, preliminary classification and event prioritisation.

layers.name: AI intelligence
layers.d: Deep learning, computer vision, anomaly detection, time-series modelling, multi-agent reinforcement learning, sensor fusion and predictive modelling.

layers.name: Environmental intelligence
layers.d: Environmental and hazard maps, risk scores, temporal trends, alerts and predicted hazard trajectories.

layers.name: Decision support
layers.d: A dashboard with live UAV positions, observations, hazard locations, risk levels, historical comparisons and recommended monitoring priorities.

stages.name: Foundation
stages.d: Environmental requirements, system architecture, sensor selection, datasets, baseline AI models and prototype development.

stages.name: AI and edge intelligence
stages.d: Environmental computer vision, sensor fusion, edge-AI optimisation and anomaly detection.

stages.name: Swarm intelligence
stages.d: Multi-agent reinforcement learning, autonomous task allocation, route optimisation and energy-aware coordination.

stages.name: Environmental intelligence
stages.d: Environmental mapping, prediction, early-warning system and dashboard development.

stages.name: Demonstration
stages.d: Controlled and field-oriented testing, performance evaluation, system refinement and industrial validation.

stages.name: Translation
stages.d: Prototype maturity, deployment assessment, technology-transfer planning, publications, IP assessment and commercialisation strategy.

risks.m: Edge processing, local autonomy and decentralised swarm coordination.
Energy-aware routing, dynamic task allocation and coordinated UAV replacement.
Multi-sensor fusion, confidence estimation, model validation and human oversight.

risks.w: Wind, rain, smoke or extreme weather disrupts flights.
risks.m: Weather-aware mission planning and adaptive deployment.

risks.w: AI models are too heavy for onboard hardware.
risks.m: Lightweight architectures, compression, quantisation and hardware-aware optimisation.
